posts.text:
Choosing between Spring Boot and Quarkus for a new service often comes down to your team's existing familiarity rather than raw performance gains. Spring Boot is the standard for most enterprise teams, making the hiring process and internal support straightforward. You get an massive ecosystem that handles almost any integration requirement out of the box.

Quarkus shines when you prioritize fast startup times and low memory footprints in containerized environments. It feels right at home if your team already knows Jakarta EE or prefers a more opinionated path for Kubernetes-native deployments. The trade-off is often a smaller pool of community solutions for niche edge cases. Before switching frameworks, measure whether your deployment cycle is actually constrained by startup speed or if the real bottleneck is simply how your team writes and maintains business logic.

📌 Strengthening One Health governance, securing sustainable domestic financing, and clarifying how agencies will track progress and be held accountable for implementing national AMR action plans.
📌 Strengthening surveillance and information sharing to address the cross-border spread of resistant organisms, including through food supply chains and the environment.
📌 Building on existing regional mechanisms to conduct joint risk assessments and develop shared priorities ahead of the 2029 UN High-Level Meeting on AMR.

The dialogue brought together country delegations and international partners, including WHO, GARDP, ICARS and the ASEAN–UK Health Security Partnership. We appreciated the opportunity to exchange experiences with colleagues from across the region and discuss where we can work together.
